newsitem.title: JAPAN: Racketeer deals with brokerages not confirmed--MOF.
newsitem.headline: Racketeer deals with brokerages not confirmed--MOF.

text.p: Japanese Finance Minister Hiroshi Mitsuzuka said on Tuesday that the ministry had not confirmed media reports that three more major brokerages had illegal stock deals with the racketeer at the centre of the Nomura scandal.

Media reports said on Monday that "sokaiya" racketeer Ryuichi Koike had told prosecutors that Nikko Securities Co Ltd, Daiwa Securities Co Ltd and Yamaichi Securities Co Ltd had made discretionary stock deals for him.
Mitsuzuka told reporters that the ministry had no independent confirmation of the reports but added that Japan's securities watchdog would deal appropriately with any wrongdoing.
Discretionary deals by brokerages on behalf of customers are banned by Japan's Securities Law as they can be used to illegally compensate clients for losses on stock trades.
Koike is at the centre of the high-profile payoff scandal involving Dai-Ichi Kangyo Bank Ltd and Nomura Securities Co Ltd.

"We have not confirmed the facts which have been reported in the media. However, if other securities firms had discretionary deals, I am sure that the Securities and Exchange Surveillance Commission will deal with it appropriately," Mitsuzuka said.

Mitsuzuka reiterated that the ministry will deal severely with DKB over its links to Koike, but said that MOF also had to take into account small- and medium-sized firms which depend on the bank for borrowings and deposits.
"This is an important point to consider when we are dealing severely with the bank. I am agonising about how to keep the balance," Mitsuzuka said.
He was responding to a question about whether the ministry's priority will be the severity of the punishment or the protection of depositors.
